question: What happens to jointly owned property when one co-owner dies?

branches.legal_effect: The deceased joint tenant's interest ceases on death and the surviving joint tenant(s) take by survivorship, subject to the applicable legal framework.
branches.registration_route: Land Registration Rules 2012, Rule 94; LR Form 47
branches.evidence: Proof of death and identity; prescribed registration application.

branches.legal_effect: The deceased co-owner's undivided share does not pass automatically to the other co-owner(s); it passes through the deceased's succession/estate framework.
branches.registration_route: Applicable transmission/devolution procedure under the Land Registration Rules.
branches.evidence: Will/probate or intestacy documentation and title evidence as applicable.

guardrails: Do not assume survivorship without establishing joint tenancy.
Do not assume a deceased tenant-in-common share passes to the surviving co-owner.
Do not treat the folio alone as resolving beneficial ownership or trust issues.
Registration after death is distinct from the underlying succession entitlement.
